instruction: find a free-standing chair, walk to it and sit down in it
safety_notes: Walk up to the chair in short moves and never walk into it.

Sitting is the onboard controller's sit straight down: line up square in front of the chair while you can see it, then turn around and back up as the sit tool says. A 180-degree turn never ends exactly, and once turned away the camera cannot see the chair: look back over a shoulder (look 145 or -145) to check the alignment before backing up and again before sitting, correcting with small moves.
notes: Demo 2: a chair 1.5 m straight ahead of the start, facing the robot (its seat's front edge about 1.28 m away). The model is not told where it is: it finds it in the camera, walks about 0.8 m, turns around, looks back to check, backs up 0.3 m and sits. Needs HF_TOKEN. Twin: g1 run sit_in_the_chair --sim (the twin sits; it does not play the stand-up, so the run ends seated with a warning). Robot: put a chair about 1.5 m in front of it, facing it, with clear floor between; --mode standing only, with a spotter and the remote ready; the teardown stands it up with SetFsmId(801). Before the first robot run, try the sit by hand with a chair already behind the heels (a tools task: {"tools": "sit"}).
